walkthroughs.body_html:
Poetry Anthology Collection — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Poetry Anthology Collection brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Poetry Anthology Collection.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
A theme is the title of the book.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
Dramatic irony is when something ironic happens in a play.
Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
A theme is the title of the book.
When the audience knows something a character does not, creating tension between the character's words/actions and the audience's understanding.
